protocolDescription: A plot is placed in a stand of vegetation that is homogeneous in structure and species composition, chosen by the author (preferential placement). Plot size follows Chytrý & Otýpková (2003): 16 m² for grassland and 200 m² for woodland. Every vascular plant species in the plot is listed by layer, with a cover-abundance value and a sociability value. Bryophytes and lichens on soil, rock and dead wood (not on the bark of living trees) are listed in the moss layer when the author identifies them; whether they were identified is recorded per relevé. Layers: tree layer (woody plants taller than 5 m), shrub layer (woody plants 1-5 m), herb layer (all herbaceous plants, and woody plants below 1 m, including seedlings), moss layer (bryophytes and lichens). A species present in several layers is recorded once per layer. Cover-abundance (Barkman, Doing & Segal 1964): r = one or very few individuals, cover negligible; + = few individuals, cover below 1%; 1 = numerous individuals, cover below 5%; 2m = very numerous (more than 100 individuals), cover below 5%; 2a = any number, cover 5-12.5%; 2b = any number, cover 12.5-25%; 3 = cover 25-50%; 4 = cover 50-75%; 5 = cover 75-100%. Dropping the letters gives the classic Braun-Blanquet scale. Sociability (Braun-Blanquet 1932): 1 = growing singly; 2 = grouped or tufted; 3 = in troops, small patches or cushions; 4 = in small colonies, extensive patches or carpets; 5 = in great crowds (pure populations). Header data: aspect (compass point), inclination (degrees), total cover and cover of each layer (%), height of each layer, whether bryophytes and lichens were identified, and bedrock. Species seen in the same stand outside the plot may be listed separately, without values.
protocolReferences: Braun-Blanquet, J. (1932). Plant Sociology. McGraw-Hill. | Barkman, J. J., Doing, H. & Segal, S. (1964). Acta Botanica Neerlandica 13: 394-419. | Chytrý, M. & Otýpková, Z. (2003). Journal of Vegetation Science 14: 563-570.

protocolDescription: After fieldwork, the author assigns each relevé to an association by comparing its species composition with the diagnostic species of the associations recognised in the regional vegetation overview. Syntaxon names follow the International Code of Phytosociological Nomenclature.
protocolRemarks: An interpretation of the relevé made after fieldwork, not a field observation.
